title.narrative: Initiative Africa 2018-2024, Making Change Happen 2 - Business for Peace
Initiative Africa 2018-2024, Making Change Happen 2 - Business for Peace

description.narrative:
Phase I implemented between 2018-2020 The project aims to bridge the gap between civics and peace building activities especially involving the private sector. It takes a two-pronged approach that includes: (a) development of several civic education programs as a tool for peace-building; and (b) enhancement of capacity of business to handle complex conflict subject matter, especially in relation to social inequality and justice. The following objectives are identified: 1. To mobilize the business community to engage in peace-building and conflict resolution actions and activities. 2. Through corporate social responsibility to maintain support for effective peace building and inclusive coordination amongst Government, private sector, media actors and civil society. 3. To respond to concrete challenges and opportunities to build a peaceful and just Ethiopia through civic education, training, internship and apprenticeship activities.
Phase II - Business for Peace, implementation period 2021-2023 This second phase aims to integrate and implement a peace building program to encourage Ethiopia's business community to positively influence the course of peace-making around the nation. The expanded objectives added to the approved MCH are: 1) To mobilize the business community to engage in peace building and conflict resolution actions and activities. 2) Through corporate social responsibility to maintain support for effective peace building and inclusive coordination amongst Government, private sector, media actors and civil society. 3) To respond to concrete challenges and opportunities to build a peaceful and just Ethiopia through civic education, training, internship, and apprenticeship activities.

Det övergripande målet för denna andra fas är att föra den privata sektorn till bordet och utveckla vägar för politisk dialog för att uppnå praktiska och fredliga lösningar på problem. Tanken är att företag ska hjälpa till att bevara sociala och medborgerliga strukturer genom att fortsätta göra affärer över olika konfliktgränser och arbeta tillsammans med andra civilsamhällesgrupper. Genom att arbeta med regeringen och olika delar av civilsamhällets organisationer på ett informerat och deltagande sätt, syftar projektet också till att förbättra utsikterna för jämställd och hållbar fred mellan könen.

The overall objective of this second phase is to bring the private sector to the table and develop avenues for political dialogue to achieve practical and peaceful solutions to problems. The idea is for business to help in preserving social and civic fabric by continuing to do business across different conflict lines and work together with other civil society groups. By working with the Government and the different segments of civil society organizations in an informed, participatory manner, the project also aims to improve the prospects for gender-equitable and sustainable peace.

Phase I Major achievements include the Ministry of Education's decision to use the School Violence Index, SVI, that was developed by IA to measure gender based violence in school settings across the country. This is a major endorsement from the government's side to take forward good practices to improve the safety of students.
Other achievements include the rapid assessment on SGBV increasing trends during the pandemic, gender audit of print media as well as the production of videos showcasing successful women in different areas of work and academia. These particular videos have been shared on the Embassy social media and had received one of the highest views and reaction.
IA had already been engaged in voter education with the proper licensing from the National election board of Ethiopia before the House of Federation postponed the national elections. There was a field visit conducted on the first quarter of 2020 where we had the opportunity to witness a training held for first time voters in a high school in Hawassa. The cooperation partner was able to use different tools to gauge level of interests from participants and use the occasion to discuss other issues of participation that the youth were facing.
Seen how the cooperation partner rose up to the challenge of adapting to fluid context, Sweden believed that extending the programme with a slightly different focus was necessary. As such a decision was taken to extend the programme with the main focus on facilitating peace building and dialogue with the engagement of the business community especially in conflict ridden areas.
Phase II key impact level achieved in the second phase includes; 1. The contribution was instrumental in helping businesses more specifically and private sector associations in general, to be motivated to rethink and redesign their engagement in peace building initiatives, 2. Partnership and platforms forged with key institutions will serve a catalytic role in bringing organized voices of the private sector, 3. the program supported the creation of knowledge and demonstrate information established and analyzed at the local level, 4. Business membership organizations (BMOs) have demonstrated that they are embedding the work of peace into the works of their associations and have now begun to proactively engage in this space
Key results achievement assessed to be made with this contribution include; I. The conclusive and remarkable effect of the project is an improved understanding of the role businesses can play in peace building among key and influential institutions. II. The contribution has helped a formalized strategic partnership with the Ministry of Peace, the National Dialogue Commission (NDC) and National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC) to strengthen and facilitate private sector engagement in peace building and rehabilitation efforts. III. Technical assistance provided to support business associations to work with their members to integrate peace building strategies into their operations and CSR activities, including a catered support to the Addis Ababa Chamber of Commerce and Sectoral Association to organize a consecutive platform to launch a city-wide discussion on national dialogue and peace building. This has created an opportunity to launch the Ethiopia Global compact program. IV. Selected business leaders have acquired and used proven skills on how to integrate peace issues into their business plans with policy paper presentations to recommend strategic directions and solutions. V. Supported national, regional and local level platforms to convene private and public actors in one space. The platforms has envisioned regional expansion to look at cross-border and cross-cultural themes focused on Business and Peace, VI. initiated and supported the first two cohorts of Business and peace building fellowship programs in partnership with the institute for Peace and Security Studies (IPSS) of Addis Ababa University. VII. The partnership between Initiative Africa and Institute for Security Studies (ISS) has given ISS the opportunity to do outreach to the Ethiopian private sector in local peace building. The collaboration has led to research pieces to understand and build a body of knowledge on Business and Peace.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
